name: 3a55a80127ba22edae8bc7c80fa85b9d

Smart helmets have to survive real-life conditions:
rain, sweat, potholes, heat, cold, daily vibration, and thousands of power cycles.

name: 46c0ddc756cfe5e12faafd239fe67703

Certifications are the minimum standard.

name: 61eb4f74ff0f8029f6b2eaec0a73e156

Because we don’t make traditional helmets.
We design Active Safety systems, and that requires a different level of engineering, testing, and transparency.

name: a2489b18ffd43c67b4b8a771f75e8cdd
source: When a brand hides its factory, testing methods, or quality process, you should ask why.

name: b8e33f43d606975688280197ac4812ee

A helmet shouldn’t pass one lab test and call it a day.
It should consistently survive the way real riders use it.

name: bc90b606b63ab181eed6e6407f72c129
source:
The video doesn’t show “content.”
It shows proof — real engineering, real testing, real quality control.

name: c4016357abcb9a63c2aeb7e54d89454f
source:
Helmet protection begins long before final assembly.
In this episode of UNIT 1 Labs, we show how our shells are formed, trimmed, and prepared for bonding. The process includes:

name: c53653c7ad0f3587c49daa93f6fb2b37
source:
Most helmet brands talk about “quality,” but almost none show what that actually means.
That’s why we opened our factory and documented every step of how a UNIT 1 helmet is built. Because the truth is simple: not all helmets are alike, and how they’re made determines how well they protect you.

name: d1aea79f4e41636f22fe4ef496f28fee
source:
EPS foam is the core material that absorbs impact.
If its density is even slightly off, the helmet won’t perform properly in a crash.

name: e3d824694dc09f10e2666b356de40b4e
source:
Most helmets only undergo standard impact tests.
Smart helmets require more... a lot more.

name: 0f2a1eb19ac4e05d0c81bf5393c078f4
source: EN 1078: Europe’s standard. Same concept with impact and strap tests, but not as strict when it comes to high-speed crashes.

name: 12b6510b836ae9eae501cadcdcc08e41
source: Hits against flat surfaces and curb-like edges

name: 15ad0e46a4f18ce93604d4f1156cf0db
source: Simple star ratings - 5 stars means excellent protection, 2 stars means… maybe don’t.

name: 2b2d31f2c186df28a77871d0ab356a6a
source: Here’s the quick breakdown of the big three:

name: 2fb22a3730804fdb84bc14feba7d9c26
source: Why their STAR (Summation of Tests for the Analysis of Risk) rating system matters:

name: 3590c222f5bc7d3afd3dd2a4e021b626
source: CPSC (Consumer Product Safety Commission): The US baseline. If a helmet is sold in the States, it meets this. Think of it like the "you must be this tall to ride" sign at a theme park. It’s the minimum bar.

name: 44deb2573d8d0d670f91285e9ce85cba
source: How to Pick Your Next Helmet Without Regrets

name: 4756c9e6a19f691a7fc078db4667b956
source: Match your ride style - Commuter? Get more coverage and visibility. Road warrior? Go for maximum ventilation. Night rider? That’s where AURA and NEON Smart Helmets shine (literally).

name: 52cc4e48a3a529be75d45fb8b02e5e97
source: Protect four key impact zones (including your temples and the back of your head)

name: 617df9d390315a44c87f7feb84208a83
source: Your brain isn’t replaceable. Your helmet should protect it like treasure.

name: 621f9bda1aebb9879c4f55db6bc1a332
source: That’s why the NTA 8776 standard matters so much. It ensures helmets can:

name: 67b6dd6b6ae6d77a508891e27da3c5da
source: Find rotational impact protection - Features like MIPS, WaveCel, or SPIN help with sideways crashes.

name: 6e30d7f3eb2c752165eba19b26132438
source: What is the Virginia Tech Helmet Rating and How Does it Work?

name: 6f1ca871fb3c8d1f9ddb0e21ad73bed6
source: Hold up in heat, cold, rain, and UV

name: 7111beae1261c06b47728d762adc250a
source: Handle harder hits at higher speeds

name: 76cea7c36b50685405e2625af1ecb01b
source: Extra coverage for temples and the back of your head (the spots you really don’t want meeting asphalt.)

name: 7ee2e0fbe5acff0f013d2bc756665e6b
source: So when you’re weighing CPSC vs EN 1078 vs the NTA 8776 standard, remember this: if you’re going fast on an e-bike, NTA 8776 is your non-negotiable. But not all helmets are created equal. Some just squeak by the minimum test. Others go way beyond. That’s where Virginia Tech’s helmet ratings swoop in to save the day.

name: a3d61026bbaec467c05bdc7cf3f95d50
source: Shameless plug: our AURA smart helmet doesn’t just meet NTA 8776. It’s rocking a 5-star Virginia Tech helmet rating, ranked #17 overall, #3 in the urban category, and it’s officially the highest-ranked smart helmet on the list. Safe, stylish, and lit up like a spaceship.

name: a595578d7bc34dc85d238a9988512859

name: a962268f77b18513afc754bc266d9b73
source: Let’s be real: buying a helmet can feel like shopping for avocados at the grocery store. They all look good on the outside. But which one is actually ripe enough to protect your brain when things get sketchy?

name: aaef1da1410ad2278ec836da59810b58
source: Riding a traditional road bike is one thing. Riding an e-bike or speed pedelec is another story. At 25 to 28 mph (that’s roughly 40 to 45 km/h, or 6.3 m/s in test terms) the stakes are way higher. A regular CPSC or EN 1078 helmet just isn’t built for those speeds.

name: b5cf9fba3be36f066daafd2dbd02f81b
source: Check the certification - CPSC if you’re in the US, EN 1078 in Europe, and definitely NTA 8776 if you ride an e-bike.

name: baebbb97904d2726656b84266e150c37
